answer_1.quote: Long-form question answering, an emerging research area within QA, requires systems to generate long and complex answers to questions by leveraging large language models and evidence document retrievers.
answer_1.outputs: long and complex answers to questions

answer_2.quote: We curate a suite of 12 automatic metrics and measure how they correlate to human judgments of both "overall quality" and two fine-grained aspects (coherence and faithfulness).

answer_3.quote: We experiment with pretrained T5 checkpoints of different sizes (220M, 770M, 3B, and 11B parameters) on our task zero-shot.
methods: zero-shot disambiguation of masked answer references in justifications

answer_4.quote: We hire domain experts in seven different fields (e.g., biology, economics) to perform the same answer preference task and additionally provide detailed justifications as to why they chose a particular answer.
answer_4.guideline: Given a question and two candidate answers, the experts were asked to choose which of the answers is better (overall preference), indicate whether the decision was difficult to make, and lastly to justify their choice in a free-form paragraph.
